newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian housing recovery uneven - industry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian housing recovery uneven - industry.

text.p: Australia's housing industry said official data released on Tuesday showed the housing industry was recovering but signalled the upturn was patchy. "Despite the large increase in the total number of dwellings approved, the housing recovery remains uneven," Master Builders Australia said in a statement.
Official data released earlier on Tuesday showed housing approvals increased 10.4 percent, seasonally-adjusted, in January from the previous month.
But Master Builders and the Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) contrasted the 0.5 percent fall in private sector house approvals against the 36.7 percent increase in "other residential" units.
"The increase in building approvals in January did not...extend across the entire housing market," REIA president Don Brindley said in a statement.
"REIA has predicted that the current upswing in the property market will be much less dramatic than the the late 1980s upturn."
The Housing Industry Association said reductions in mortgage interest rates were beginning to lure home-buyers back into the residential market.
"The trend estimate of private dwelling approvals, a measure of underlying movements, is now moving upwards," association managing director Ron Silberberg said in a statement.
But Master Builders Australia said the increase in total approvals was due to increased high rise apartments and major townhouse developments.
Approvals for private sector houses showed "that the expected pick-up in new housing activity as a result of the recent cuts in interest rates has not yet become apparent".
The REIA said the upturn was being held back by relatively low consumer confidence.
"Also, compulsory superannuation and Higher Education Contribution Scheme repayments are making it harder for young consumers to save for a deposit on their first home," Brindley said.
